title: BitMEX to shut down exchange operations on Sept. 23
summary: BitMEX said it will shut down exchange operations at 4:00 a.m. UTC on Sept. 23 after a strategic review of its business and the cryptocurrency industry.The exchange said new account registrations were suspended immediately, and users must close positions and withdraw assets before the shutdown. Starting at 4:00 a.m. UTC on Aug. 26, users will no longer be able to open new positions and will only be allowed to reduce existing ones. Any open positions remaining before the shutdown will be forcibly liquidated by the time operations end, and positions still on the books at the cutoff will be liquidated immediately, BitMEX said. After the shutdown, users will still be able to log in, check balances and withdraw assets, but trading services will no longer be available.BitMEX added that if users who have completed KYC leave assets in their accounts after the shutdown, an account fee equal to $50 per month or 1% annually, whichever is greater, will apply.Founded in 2014, BitMEX is a first-generation derivatives exchange. Its founders are Arthur Hayes, Ben Delo and Samuel Reed. Since 2020, the company has faced pressure including lawsuits from the U.S. Department of Justice and the CFTC. After losing its lead in the derivatives market to later entrants including Binance, Bybit and OKX after 2014, BitMEX pursued a sale, but no deal was completed.

title: Seven Democratic senators oppose revised CLARITY Act
summary: Seven Democratic U.S. senators have also voiced opposition to a revised version of the CLARITY Act that adds ethics rules for public officials, increasing uncertainty over whether the bill can pass before the August recess, according to BeInCrypto. Sens. Catherine Cortez Masto, Angela Alsobrooks, Cory Booker, Ruben Gallego, John Hickenlooper, Mark Warner and Raphael Warnock said the bill still needs stronger provisions on consumer protection, illicit finance prevention and market integrity, not just ethics rules. Banking industry groups also said deposit risks remain a concern and argued the revised bill could still curb regional lending. Compared with the draft released in May, the revised version newly adds ethics rules restricting public officials from issuing or endorsing cryptocurrencies, as well as law enforcement provisions allowing the seizure of stablecoins. It keeps the existing framework under which the SEC and CFTC share oversight of cryptocurrencies.

summary: Kazakhstan has approved rules for a strategic digital mining program that guarantee electricity supplies to cryptocurrency mining companies for up to 10 years, according to a report by a West Asian media outlet. Under the rules, participating companies can receive power allocations from electricity generators at capped rates. In return, they must transfer part of their mined cryptocurrency to Kazakhstan’s Silicon Valley, Astar Network, or a hub, and the assets will be held in trust by a state investment corporation under the central bank before being used to expand the country’s strategic crypto reserve.
